newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end weaker, back away from three-yr high.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end weaker, back away from three-yr high.

text.p: * NZ shares end weaker, index fails to breach three-yr high
* Offshore buyers take a break on the day but may return
* Peters' comments on rise in NZ dollar "toothless"
138 nil * NZSE-40 cap index -7.70 at 2,432.51 340 +1 * NZSC cap index -1.01 at 5,205.91
297 -1 * NZSE-10 cap index -4.43 at 1,216.08 360 -5 * Volume NZ$42 million. Futures -10 at 1,220
New Zealand shares closed weaker on Tuesday after initially looking set to break through a three-year high and post fresh resistance levels.
"There was not the same depth of buying that we've seen in the last few days," said Phil Hardie Boys at BZW.

The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 7.70 points lower at 2,432.51. Early in the session, the index had gained a couple of points to eye 2,444.80, a three-year high set in February 1994. If it breaches that resistance level, it will be at its highest point since September 1989.

But a sluggish performance by leading stocks in afternoon trade put paid to any bullish aspirations. Telecom ended four cents weaker at NZ$7.52, while Lion Nathan dipped five to $3.60. Brokers said offshore buying, which has recently been driving the market higher, had simply not eventuated.
"The market just backed away from doing a lot of buying today. The thing with the offshore guys is they do come and go a wee bit. They may be back tomorrow, who knows," said Hardie Boys.
He said comments by Treasurer Winston Peters, who said the speed of the New Zealand dollar's rise was more of a concern than the rise itself, were of little consequence.
"Peters came out and said the rise in the dollar was too fast -- I don't think that really bothered anyone. In fact it looked a pretty toothless comment," he said.
However, the currency and interest rates had a bearing on the share market and the current furore about the strength of the Kiwi dollar was probably not helping equities.
